questions.stem: Why might plant roots in waterlogged soil die if conditions persist?

options.text: The roots absorb too much water and burst
Toxic ethanol builds up from anaerobic respiration
The soil becomes too acidic from carbon dioxide
The roots cannot absorb minerals from wet soil

questions.explanation: In waterlogged soil, roots cannot access oxygen and switch to anaerobic respiration, producing ethanol. Ethanol is toxic and accumulates over time, which can kill the root cells.
